content.text: {"vat": "Tall black crowned hat worn by a man walking in the street (headgear)", "dac_diem": "The hat is dark and tall with a flat top, a slightly tapered crown and a narrow brim. It looks like a plain, buckle-less sugarloaf or capotain hat. The man also wears a long dark coat with a belt and dark boots. The image is blurry, so I can't make out a hat band or buckle.", "co_tu_nam": 1590, "da_co_nam_1680": "yes", "ly_do": "Tall-crowned black hats (capotain/sugarloaf style) were worn in England from about the late 16th century, and Puritan-style plain versions were still common around 1680. Nothing visible, such as a top-hat silhouette or a buckle, points to a later design."}
